# Current165 tracking direction, velocity and heading source review

No clear active source error has been established that justifies changing the publisher, velocity goals or weights. ## The +0.5 publisher is not the selected tracking command

`native_fudan_step_bridge_v1.py:install_fudan_step_request_and_command` publishes body-forward .5 during public request and preserves the original physical task. That field appears in the original physical RewardManager/diagnostics. It is not read by the selected native actor observation or WM input.

`ConvertedMOD4JumpMdp.obs` concatenates invariant physical features, previous action and `relative_features`. Encoder bias is from the episode-static context. `OwnFudanStepMdp.obs` replaces one redundant orientation feature by .01*yaw/pi; its active `relative_features` override decodes public age and builds world target-minus-root/terrain offsets, request200..1999 and age seconds. The ancestor's legacy request100..179 and packed-frame argument are overridden here. There is no active packedframe-as-publicage or .5 velocity-command feature in that path.

`compact_episode_static31_v1` contains mass/friction/motor/COM/PD/spring/damping/lag/encoder-bias parameters, not a desired velocity. `AugmentedWheelLegWorldModel.inputs` uses invariant physical state, dynamic auxiliary state, actual action, normalized static context and terrain-relative coordinates. Its world-heading cues are derived from the current rotation; it does not read a command publisher or the reference directly.

The selected tracking loss is built in `OwnMatlabTrackingMdp.selected_tracking_terms` and returned as positive .20/(1+loss). Its root_vxy target is the reference packed columns7:9, masked by those same columns. Original13 Fudan terms are added afterwards under no_grad as diagnostics only. `NativeWheelLegBridge.step` computes `native_reward=mdp.reward(...)`, stores it as transition.r and returns it as NativeBridgeState.reward. The physical V8 reward is retained separately as `physical_V8_reward_snapshot`. Native imagination calls `mdp.reward` directly. Therefore the mere existence of the physical .5 publisher does not prove a conflict in the selected actor/WM/reward calculation. This is a direct dependency finding, not a claim that every original environment side effect is absent.

## World and body frames are explicitly different but not subtracted inconsistently

Actor invariant linear/angular velocities are R-transpose times world v/w. Its reference goal first13 slots are world p/wxyz/v/w in fixed SI units, and world target-relative offsets plus explicit yaw are observable. The selected root_vxy subtraction is world v minus world reference v; selected orientation subtracts world rotation matrices. OwnFK wheel XY/height targets use the same world/task frame. WM predicts increments in the documented heading/body frames then rotates them back into world state. These source operations do not establish an unhandled world/body subtraction error. Whether the learned policy uses these cues effectively cannot be answered from source or visual agreement alone.

## Position retiming did update packed velocities

The selected lineage is own144 builderV4 -> floor/longer ground157 -> ROOT162 push15 borrowing crouch -> new COM child -> constant-H child -> copied165 goal table. The source preparation pins the final reference as3768257B/SHA5ce19f0fe91f60cc835d714214207d491c4ebbcb641fe8201d9314d7e7bb75a2, copied to `source/OWN_MATLAB162_CONSTANT_H_GOAL_ONLY_REFERENCE.json`.

`solve_own_ground_floor_reference157_once.m` rebuilds the complete table and writes8:10 from position finite differences,11:13 from quaternion finite differences and44:73 from q differences while preserving physicaldq masks0. The push-retime source again globally recomputes8:10 and11:13 after changing q/p/timing. COM repair updates air root positions and explicitly assigns analytic COM velocity minus reference COM-offset FD to8:10. Constant-H repair changes air R and root p, explicitly writes integrated world omega to11:13, and recomputes8:10 as desired COMv minus the new rotated-offset FD. Ground values outside these edits are inherited from the preceding full-table recomputation. Contact/takeoff boundary velocity masks are zeroed, and physicaldq masks remain0. Thus a blanket stale-root-velocity hypothesis is not supported by this producer chain. FD/R-ODE discrepancies and phase-boundary stitching require numerical interpretation rather than a source-based assumption of unchanged old fields.

ROOT174 reports same-time orange versus actual packed goal position agreement within5.92e-8m and phase-interior rootv/position-FD error mean2.19e-7/max5.83e-6m/s; rootomega/Rdot error mean2.67e-5/max.0272rad/s. ROOT also reports endpoint publicages1..1046 at .01s without a gross HUD clock offset. These are attributed existing diagnostics, not new author reads or a proof of motor/physical attainability.

## Orientation exists, but its mask is phase dependent

The builderV4 initializes root1:13 masks to1, then sets quaternion4:7 mask0 for phase6/7. Ground157 copies age200 mask1 for its entire retimed age200..coast_end segment. Push retiming does not clear those ground masks or regenerate every orientation mask from its new phase labels. COM repair clears the geometric air interval's quaternion mask; constant-H does not reopen it, even though it computes an attitude. The air quaternion is therefore still unknown/masked for conditioning and selected orientation loss.

The selected `ground_orientation` formula is not multiplied by the `ground` phase flag; it is multiplied by `mask[...,3:7].amin`. Consequently it is wrong both to say there is no heading loss and to say it is active at every phase. Backoff/brake/acceleration/coast have an active world-R target by the producer source, while planned air is masked. An actual robot that has not taken off can still arrive at a reference phase with orientation mask0. This is an explicit task choice/coverage issue, not evidence that the earlier observed ground turning was caused by an absent ground orientation target. No mask is changed in this review.

The representation also has an acknowledged wrapped-yaw seam at +/-pi. The reported actual excursion to90.2011degrees is not by itself that seam. ROOT174 reports mean absolute heading error40.5244degrees and same-time XY mean.515555m/max1.103788m: the observed policy fails tracking despite the source offering those signals. We do not infer a weight or optimization fix from the magnitude alone.

## Minimum next discriminating evidence

ROOT173 has now reconstructed all28/80 first blue STOPs as hard closure, with tilt/timeout/unresolved0 and max head difference5.96e-8; float32/64 reason masks agreed. Gray's only >2mm endpoint was the last one,2.107555mm. The imaginary closed-loop actions differ after the first shared action, so this is not an identified false positive or isolated WM error.

The next necessary model question is conditional WM closure/heading calibration under the same recorded actual actions. A separately frozen purpose can use one qualified165 WM decode and one forward pass of new172 control data, without Pi/Critic/optimizer, reference table or new physics. One-step comparisons and bounded8/32 actual-action windows must distinguish predicted FK closure/yaw from same-point native-state and cached-body labels. It must not inject future actual states or observations into the interior rollout, cross a reset, resample an actor, or call this a population accuracy campaign. The companion contract specifies this proposed scope; it is not permission or execution.

Source-only counterexamples should first test dependency and mask semantics: holding all native inputs fixed while changing only the physical publisher has no selected input change; a quarter-turn changes selected orientation at mask1, while that term and quaternion conditioning become0 at mask0. World negative-X velocity must be compared in world coordinates, with body velocity changing according to heading. These are narrow mathematical checks, not new source patches, training gates or claims of successful control. No reward, weight, observation width, publisher, norm or physical guard is changed.

# Source findings for the proposed175 diagnostic

The current165 actor decoder has a final Linear layer. `Policy.forward` applies tanh only to the encoded goal latent, then returns the decoder output without an output tanh. This is source evidence, not a measurement of the saved actor outputs.

`supermimic_wheel_leg_v3/learner.py:_imag_step` computes `action=clamp(Pi(...),-6,6)` before WM.step. The predicted observation's previous action, all saved imagined actions, the selected reward and the critic's future-state route use that clipped value. `policy_update` minimizes minus the discounted survival-weighted reward plus terminal critic objective. Its selected policy-loss route contains no separate penalty on the unclipped mean. Tracking `action_rate` receives clipped actions; its nominal-overrequest helper clamps again. The output-to-action edge therefore has local derivative zero strictly outside +/-6. At the exact boundary, report a kink separately instead of assigning an inferred outside status.

This does not mean every policy parameter has zero gradient or that the policy cannot change. Other rows, axes and steps share parameters; other action/state routes and optimizer state can move the output. A report showing all20 parameter tensors nonzero does not establish a nonzero derivative for each action row/axis. Conversely, saved physical-case saturation alone is not proof of saturation in the training imagination states, nor a causal explanation of the tracking failure.

The actual NEW172 driver records four distinct vectors. It saves the unbounded mean6, sends mean.clamp(-20,20) as raw_native_clamp20_6, caches action_manager.action as terminal.state.executed6, and separately caches delayed processed queue values as physical_applied_processed6. The native bridge stores cached executed6 as transition.a. Same-action WM calibration must use this ingress action, matching the transition contract. It must not use the processed PD targets, pretend those targets are torques, or clamp the actual executed input to +/-6 merely because imagination uses that bound. The same-read saturation report should retain all four vectors without merging their action orders.

Only source was read for this protocol. No model/raw/NPZ/reference/numerical diagnostic was executed or read by the author. The proposed input-producing purpose must be frozen by ROOT before the one necessary model decode and one necessary NEW172 control read. The protocol does not approve execution or alter any plant/reward/threshold. Preserve the existing actual173 finding that28 closed-loop branches first stopped on predicted hard closure, while one real172 terminal endpoint exceeded the original threshold; different future actions prevent labeling those28 as false positives.
